AI Summit 2026 — immersive room handoff

Everything needed to render, play back, change or take over the DX Trading Floor immersive content. Written for three readers: the AV team running the room, the designer who picks this up next, and whoever has to answer "why is it like that?" in six months.

The companion document is README.md, which covers the same ground in more depth and from the code's side. This file is the operational one.

1. Deliverables and status

Piece Spec Status
Convergence 6878 × 1080, 3:00, seamless loop source complete, not rendered
Convergence (dark) same, walls receded for presentations source complete, not rendered
Arrival 6878 × 1080, 0:12, one shot source complete, not rendered
Name badges 4 categories, layered PDF, 5.8125 × 7.5 in artboard delivered

2. Three things to settle before rendering

1. Pixel format — this one blocks the render. Measured like-for-like on this content, 4:4:4 is both higher quality and smaller than 4:2:0:

Encode PSNR vs source Size (3 min)
yuv420p CRF 16 36.6 dB ~520 MB
yuv444p CRF 16 41.7 dB ~428 MB

Saturated brand colour on near-black is the worst case for chroma subsampling, so the encoder spends bits on the residual. The catch is that H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive decodes in software (VLC, Resolume, ffmpeg-based media servers) but not on every hardware decoder. Ask the venue what the playback machine is. If there is any doubt, render 4:2:0 — it is the default and it is universally safe.

2. Speaker names are baked into the render, not live text. Each name needs its own file. Before rendering, the production needs: the speaker list, their role lines, and whether names ride the loop all evening or only around their own session. If names change on the night there is no way to update them without a re-render, so if that is a risk, run the room without names and put them on the domino screen instead.

3. Two items carried from the concept review, both needing sign-off:

  • The Vector mark in Arrival keeps its magenta arrow. Magenta is out of the room's palette, but the mark is the mark — repainting it would be the brand error rather than the restraint. If marketing wants it gone, the all-white knockout lockup is also official and it is a one-line change.
  • The badges carry texture, against the review's "smooth gradients on badges, textured for large format". It is much lighter than the version that note was written about and it is held off the type, but it is a deliberate departure and was requested after the review.

3. Playback spec
Resolution 6878 × 1080
Frame rate 30 fps (--fps 60 available)
Codec H.264 High, CRF 16, preset slow
Pixel format yuv420p default, yuv444p optional — see §2
Colour BT.709 primaries / transfer / matrix, limited range
GOP 30 frames (1 s), fixed, scene-cut detection off
Audio none

The short fixed GOP is deliberate: it keeps seeking and loop restarts snappy on venue playback hardware, and it guarantees every segment opens on a keyframe.

Convergence loops seamlessly. The loop has been verified pixel-identical at the seam — frame at t=0 and frame at t=180 differ by zero bytes. No crossfade is needed or wanted; a crossfade will visibly soften the one frame it touches.

Arrival does not loop. It ends on a hold, which is there so it can sit under an introduction and be cut away from on a cue. Looping it will snap the lockup back to an empty room.

Per-projector files can be cut from the master with --walls, giving one file per wall (2239, 1681 and 2244 px wide). Only do this if the media server cannot window a single 6878-wide source — the corners are part of the composition and a single source keeps them in register for free.

4. Running the room

The two room states

Show state is the piece: full brightness, for the reception and the breaks.

Dark state is for when someone is presenting. The walls recede so they are not competing with what is on the screen behind the stage. Mark brightness drops to 24 %, the violet in the ground to 30 %, and bloom to 26 %.

They are two files, but they are frame-for-frame identical in geometry — same scene, same deterministic seeds, same timeline. A cross-dissolve between the two at matching timecode reads as a lighting change rather than a cut. If the media server can hold both in sync, that is the nicest way to run it. If it cannot, a hard cut on a beat is fine; nothing moves except brightness.

Cue outline

Cue File Notes
Doors / reception Convergence (show) loops indefinitely
~12 s before a keynote walks on Arrival holds on the lockup at 0:12
Speaker on stage Convergence (dark) cut or dissolve from the Arrival hold
Session ends Convergence (show)

Arrival opens on the same field, the same axis and the same speeds as the loop, so cutting into it from Convergence does not show a jump. Its timeline:

Time What happens
0:00 – 0:03 the field, indistinguishable from the loop
0:03 – 0:07.2 arrows leave the travel axis and gather on the west wall
0:07.2 – 0:08.6 the solid lockup resolves out of the swarm
0:08.6 – 0:10 the wordmark arrives
0:10 – 0:12 hold

Wayfinding

Magenta is the wayfinding colour — signs and directional arrows throughout the venue. It is deliberately kept out of the immersive content so the two do not compete. The primary magenta → cobalt gradient is still in the palette module (GRADIENT_WAYFINDING in src/brand.js) for the print pieces.

5. Rebuilding from source

Requirements

  • Node 18+ — npm install (canvas, esbuild, ffmpeg-static, playwright)
  • Python 3.11+ for the badges — cairosvg pymupdf pikepdf pypdfium2 numpy pillow
  • Karbon-Semibold.otf and Karbon-Regular.otf in the repository root. They are licensed fonts and are committed here; check that is acceptable before this repo goes anywhere public.

ffmpeg comes from ffmpeg-static, so there is nothing to install system-wide.

On a machine with more than one Python, install the packages into the same interpreter you invoke — more than one python3 on PATH is the most common reason tools/badges.py fails on a fresh machine. Every command in this section was verified end to end on a clean clone.

Commands

npm install

node tools/build-preview.js            # rebuild dist/preview.html
node tools/render.js                   # Convergence, show state
node tools/render.js --dark            # Convergence, dark state
node tools/render.js --moment          # Arrival
node tools/render.js --pix-fmt yuv444p # see section 2
node tools/render.js --walls           # also cut per-projector files
node tools/render.js --duration 10     # short test render
node tools/render.js --speaker "Glenda Crisp|President & CEO,|Vector Institute"

python3 tools/badges.py                # the four badge PDFs plus a combined one
python3 tools/verify-badges.py         # contrast + layer checks, must pass
python3 tools/handoff-pdf.py           # this document as a PDF
python3 tools/build-handoff.py         # this document as a live web page

Output names itself from the mode, so the three masters do not overwrite each other:

Command Output
node tools/render.js out/vector-convergence-6878x1080.mp4
node tools/render.js --dark out/vector-convergence-dark-6878x1080.mp4
node tools/render.js --moment out/vector-arrival-6878x1080.mp4
python3 tools/badges.py out/badges/vector-badge-*.pdf + -all.pdf
python3 tools/handoff-pdf.py dist/AI-Summit-2026-handoff.pdf
python3 tools/build-handoff.py dist/handoff.html

Full option list: --fps --crf --gop --duration --workers --out --walls --pix-fmt --dark --moment --speaker.

out/ is gitignored — everything in it regenerates. The badge build is deterministic: a rerun on a clean clone reproduces the same PDFs.

Expected cost

About 25–35 minutes per 3-minute master on four cores. Frames render at full resolution across worker processes, pipe as raw RGBA into per-segment ffmpeg encoders, and are concatenated with a stream copy so nothing is re-encoded.

Previewing

Two self-contained pages, both of which open straight off disk with no server:

  • dist/handoff.html — this document with the room running live at the top of it and the badge set below. The one to send to someone who needs to see the design rather than read about it.
  • dist/preview.html — the working review tool. Same player, no prose.

Both carry each piece, a scrub track, the venue overlay, the room-state slider, speaker-name fields and a loop-seam test. The preview is exactly what gets encoded: the same scene functions drive the page and the renderer.

Earlier cuts stay viewable rather than merely recoverable:

File Version

6. The venue, and what can go where

The template is not three equal panels. All bounds were measured from DX_TradingFloor_Immersive_Template-scaled_fullSize.png and live in VENUE in src/brand.js.

Region x range Width
South wall 0 – 2239 2239
West-faced corner 2239 – 2501 262
South-faced corner 2501 – 2596 95
West wall (audience eye-line) 2596 – 4277 1681
South-faced corner 4277 – 4371 94
West-faced corner 4371 – 4634 263
North wall 4634 – 6878 2244

Hard constraints:

  • Speaker grills at y 358–488, x 430–1376 (south) and x 5481–6426 (north). Artwork behind them reads as texture at best. Nothing load-bearing here.
  • No text below y = 538 — the template marks everything below that line as background graphics only.
  • Cube line at y = 674 on the south and north walls. Below it the surface is a physical cube, not flat wall.
  • Draped fabric at the outer edges of both cubes — soft, non-flat surfaces.
  • Domino screen on the west wall, x 2633–4243, y 0–628. Flattest and brightest surface in the room; the Arrival lockup is centred on it.

Those constraints are what place the speaker names at x 1452 and x 4742 — the grills and the no-text line leave exactly one clear block per side wall, and both happen to fall on the stage side, so the names read close to the eye-line.

The composition is otherwise a continuous field with no fixed focal point, so it survives the corner wraps and the cube line without anything important being cut in half.

7. Things that will bite whoever edits this

Each of these was hit once. Longer write-ups are in README.md.

Bloom must be sized in scene units, never off the backing store. Sizing it off the backing store makes the blur a constant number of device pixels, which is a different fraction of the artwork at every render resolution — a quarter-size preview then carries four times the bloom radius of the master, and the master arrives with visibly less glow than the preview it was approved on. This is the one place where "the preview is what gets encoded" can quietly stop being true.

-colorspace bt709 only labels the stream. ffmpeg's automatic RGB→YUV conversion still uses BT.601, so tagging alone produces a file converted with one matrix and played back with another — about 4.8 dB of error, worst on exactly the saturated violet and turquoise this piece is built from. The renderer converts explicitly with a scale=…bt709… filter plus -color_range tv.

Additive marks on a violet ground walk toward magenta. The ground pre-loads the blue channel, so once blue pins at 255 every further addition only moves red and green. At the loop's mark sizes it never gets far enough to see; at Arrival's it turned the south wall pink. Arrival therefore composites normally and lets the bloom supply the glow; the loop keeps its additive field.

PyMuPDF's rasteriser ignores optional-content state — it will report that layers "work" on a file that has none. The badge verifier renders through PDFium.

PDFium caches by filename. Reusing one scratch path made every layer comparison silently compare a file with itself.

Switching a layer off in a source PDF does nothing once you place it. Illustrator writes layers as marked-content sections in the page stream, and show_pdf_page copies the stream verbatim. The first attempt at carrying the die-line across brought the old badge artwork with it, on top, hiding three layers underneath.

8. Decisions log — don't "fix" these

  • Nothing rotates. Both official arrow paths are used verbatim, and pixels and pluses are drawn axis-aligned exactly as the official patterns are constructed. Only position, scale, opacity and fill vary. This was an explicit constraint from the outset.
  • Magenta is wayfinding only, and the violet glow stop is kept on the blue side of the hue for the reason in §7.
  • The Vector mark keeps its magenta arrow in Arrival. See §2.
  • The logo does not appear in the sustained loop. A logo reveal is by definition a change of design, which the single-sustained-field direction rules out. It has its own piece instead.
  • The badge mark field uses a different seed per side. Marks on the colour panel are darker than their ground; marks on the black are lighter than theirs. Run one mark across the boundary and its polarity inverts half-way through, and the edge becomes the loudest thing on the card. Two independent fields meeting at a clean line is what reads as continuous — building one field across both, which sounds more seamless, is what makes the seam.
  • Badge mark opacity is solved, not set. A fixed opacity gives a mark on Lime nearly three times the contrast of the same mark on Cobalt.
  • The badge logo is white on all four categories. Every confirmed pairing leads with a dark colour, and white clears the 3:1 graphics floor on all of them. Straight max-contrast would flip Magenta to black, and one black lockup in a set of four reads as a mistake at a lanyard's distance.

One correction to carry forward

An earlier note in this project flagged the perspective funnel's vanishing point as possibly misplaced — sitting at the canvas centre rather than the centre of the west wall. That was wrong, and it needs no action: the throat is at x 3439 and the west wall's centre is at x 3436.5, a difference of 2.5 px in 6878.
